description: systems/eval-harness/guardrail-checkpoint.py did not attach step-03b's pass/flag/escalate result to this run's own auto-created dream-cycle eval record (eval-20260904T080934-ZIHBLJ.json). Instead it wrote the guardrails entry into an unrelated, already-completed eval record (eval-20260903T081233-OZES3F.json, tags phantom-candidate/cowork-hook, status already success). Confirmed by inspecting both files' diffs after the fact: the correct target record has an empty guardrails field and fails its own dream-004-guardrail-checkpoint-ran assertion (which reads 'from the eval record's own guardrails array, not self-reported by the workflow') even though the checkpoint genuinely ran and returned pass. Prior dream-cycle runs (08-26 through 09-03) all logged this same call as a 'silent no-op, no in-progress dream-cycle eval record to attach to' -- that assumption was wrong; the script does write somewhere, just not to the right record, and no prior cycle noticed because no one checked the diff of unrelated eval-harness files.
correction: guardrail-checkpoint.py's eval-record resolution logic needs to target the eval record matching the current workflow name + session (or the most recently created in-progress record for that workflow name), not whatever it currently resolves as 'the' active record. Until fixed, dream-cycle's own eval record will keep failing dream-004-guardrail-checkpoint-ran even on cycles where the guardrail actually ran and passed.
systemic_fix: Fixed find_most_recent_eval_record() in systems/eval-harness/guardrail-checkpoint.py to filter on data.get("status") == "in-progress" in addition to the existing name match, before sorting by 'started' descending. Previously the selector was status-blind and would attach to the most recent record with a matching workflow name regardless of whether that record was still open, so a stale already-closed record (e.g. status: success from a prior run) could get misattributed the checkpoint result while the real in-progress record for the current run was skipped. Now a record is only eligible if its own status is the harness's actual in-progress marker (confirmed via new-eval.py, which sets status: "in-progress" at record creation, and close-open-evals.py / close-eval-record.py, which move it to a terminal status). If no such open record exists for the workflow name, the function returns None and the caller's existing silent-skip path (exit 0, no error) fires as designed -- that no-op behavior was already correct and is unchanged. Verified with two simulated scenarios: (1) only a stale status=success record with matching name on disk -> function returns None, script exits 0, stale record's guardrails array is left untouched; (2) a stale success record plus a genuinely open status=in-progress record both present -> the open record correctly receives the guardrail entry and the stale record is untouched. Did not revert the misattributed entry already written into eval-20260903T081233-OZES3F.json from tonight's run -- it's a closed log record, not live state, and reverting it isn't worth the churn; left as-is.
